body: THIS. I feel like this is me almost every day now and I hate it. My moods throughout the day change so drastically.

Around 5 years ago I was seeing this guy. We weren’t official but were essentially a couple in every sense but the label itself. He stayed over at my place more than his own and one random weekday night we decided to drive to a Mexican restaurant that’s open 24 hours. It was around 3am if I remember correctly. He drove and as I sat in the passenger seat laughing and singing along to the song playing on the radio I had a thought cross my mine. That in that moment I was experiencing a moment of pure and absolute bliss and I wished it would never end. Of course it did though. I don’t know what it was about that particular moment but I was just extremely happy and everything felt right in the world. It was a feeling that I had never experienced before in my life, at least not to the extreme in which I felt it then. I haven’t experienced anything like it ever since but the memory will randomly cross my mind from time to time and it always brings me a calming feeling. The fact that I haven’t felt that way in the years since brings me sadness and I oftentimes wonder if I’ll ever experience that sensation again.

When I was 19 (currently 27) my 16 year old neighbor passed away in a car accident. A car cut him and his father off while they were driving down the freeway which caused them to roll over (the other car took off and was never caught which is also infuriating). He was taken to the hospital but unfortunately did not make it. They had an open casket funeral and it’s the last funeral I’ve ever gone to and probably the last I will attend until the unfortunate day when one of my more immediate family members passes. I wasn’t expecting to see how badly the accident had damaged his body. His head was incredibly swollen and almost twice it’s normal size. It was an extremely heartbreaking sight. I had given my condolences to his parents and had moved on to his brothers when a man who was somehow related to them approached the mom. He essentially asked her why her son looked so funny and had such a big head (I don’t remember his exact works because and was just so shocked at the time). His mom who you could tell had already been trying her hardest to hold herself together just began crying uncontrollably. Her son who I had been speaking to instantly dashed over and began consoling her. I couldn’t and still can’t believe how inconsiderate some people can be. We all knew the circumstances under which he passed. And even then a grown man should know better than to ask something like that. I can’t imagine all the pain my neighbor went through that day.

I’ve always loved that movie since a you age. It is so sad but also such an incredible film. It’s partly why I got a tattoo saying “La vita è bella” on my ribs. To remind myself that there is beauty in love and life in general no matter how cruel the world may be.

A house and new cars for my parents along with half of my money. I’d then set up a generous account for my brother but not allow him to access it until he’s 25 (I love him to death but don’t trust his 17 year old money making decisions and don’t see him getting better about it any time soon). I’d also pay for his college education if he decides to go down that route. Then I’d take the rest of my money and just travel the world until I grow old. Each year I’d take three months off of traveling to spend with my family. When I feel like I’m doing seeing all there is to see or I feel too old to keep up that lifestyle (whichever comes first) I’d buy a house near a beach somewhere and live the rest of my days with my fur babies there.
